Paragraph:
Translation: I am now unable to stand here any longer. I am forgetting myself, and my mind is reeling. I foresee only evil, O killer of the Kesi demon.

Purport: Due to his impatience, Arjuna was unable to stay on the battlefield, and he was forgetting himself on account of the weakness of his mind. Excessive attachment for material things puts a man in a bewildering condition of existence... Arjuna envisioned only unhappiness in the battlefield—he would not be happy even by gaining victory over the foe. The word nimitta is significant. When a man sees only frustration in his expectations, he thinks, 'Why am I here?' Everyone is interested in himself and his own welfare. No one is interested in the Supreme Self... Arjuna thought that his victory in the battle would only be a cause of lamentation for him.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Following the physical collapse, Arjuna experiences a severe cognitive and psychological collapse. He loses his sense of self, his spatial awareness, and descends into purely catastrophic thinking.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna states his inability to endure the situation, reports cognitive disorientation ('forgetting myself', 'mind reeling'), and predicts an entirely negative outcome regardless of victory. The purport traces this cognitive distortion back to excessive material attachment.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna reaches a state of total despair and disorientation, entirely detached from his duty and reality.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Moha (Profound illusion or bewilderment that causes one to forget their true spiritual identity and duty)
Ajnana (Ignorance; incorrectly calculating self-interest based purely on material outcomes rather than spiritual obedience)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna has completely succumbed to Moha (illusion). By 'forgetting himself,' he has forgotten his eternal spiritual identity and his relationship with the Supreme. When disconnected from the Supreme Self, the soul can only foresee suffering ('evil') in the material world, rendering any material victory hollow.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This represents the cognitive peak of a traumatic stress response. Arjuna is experiencing depersonalization ('forgetting myself') and profound cognitive distortion. His catastrophizing ('I foresee only evil') reveals a state of complete hopelessness, where his brain cannot process any positive outcome, indicating a total breakdown of psychological resilience.
